Actual publisher markup retrieved 2026-09-06 using curl. listing.html contains verbatim selected branch-marker and event-link excerpts from https://sfpl.org/events; detail.html contains a verbatim event-article excerpt from https://sfpl.org/events/2026/09/08/tutorial-meet-one-one-financial-counselor; calendar.ics is the full https://sfpl.org/sfpl-events/add-to-calendar/162171 response. Tests mutate these fixtures explicitly to exercise missing/cancelled cases. The published date display lacks AM/PM; calendar UTC times are authoritative. Coordinates are dynamically joined by the publisher's branch URL, never geocoded or guessed.

cancelled-title.html is the verbatim h1 excerpt retrieved 2026-09-06 from https://sfpl.org/events/2026/09/06/social-afternoon-board-games. It demonstrates the publisher's actual "Canceled:" title convention, independently of ICS STATUS.

Live verification on 2026-09-07 UTC also confirmed calendar URL node ID → UID correspondence for `/sfpl-events/add-to-calendar/106394` → `106394@sfpl.org` (https://sfpl.org/events/2026/09/07/storytime-toddlers) and `/sfpl-events/add-to-calendar/112116` → `112116@sfpl.org` (https://sfpl.org/events/2026/09/07/storytime-babies). Together with saved calendar.ics this supports stable title-cancellation tombstones even without remaining dates or geometry. An event with neither a calendar link nor UID cannot safely produce the matching tombstone.

The listing's `date-end-after` parameter uses the exact current San Francisco wall time, following the publisher's observed query format (`2026-09-06 17:19:19`); midnight would allow already-ended events to exhaust the bounded detail budget.

free-policy.html is a verbatim line excerpt from the same 2026-09-06 https://sfpl.org/events download. Only presence of its explicit “All programs and events are free and open to the public.” statement permits free pricing in collected records.

HTML fixture line endings and trailing whitespace are normalized for version control.

Monthly collection was verified against live publisher HTML on 2026-09-07 UTC. `date-from=2026-09-08 00:00:00&date-to=2026-09-08 23:59:59` returns 25 event links on its first page and publisher `rel="next"` links to pages 1 and 2 with both date filters retained. Using bare dates for both filters incorrectly returns an empty midnight-only interval. The event listing is identified by `view-id-events`; an empty result explicitly contains `class="view-empty"` and `No events found. Try changing your search criteria.` (observed with the 2036-01-01 query). Tests combine these observed structures with existing selected event/branch fixtures; synthetic page links and dates are deliberate test transformations.

`collectionWindowDays: 30` opts into checking every Pacific calendar date from today through today + 29, using the full wall-time interval on each date. Two workers paginate and process days independently, with a default 200-request budget per day (`maxRequestsPerDay`, maximum 2000), a 30-page guard per day, and response caching within one run. The old `maxDetailPages` first-page budget only applies outside monthly mode. Any failed, malformed, or truncated day fails the monthly source refresh, allowing the refresh pipeline to preserve previous source data without asserting new coverage. Every listing page, including an empty result, must also echo both requested wall timestamps in its `date-from` and `date-to` input values; a publisher page that ignores the date filters fails safely. Only a fully successful month returns authoritative `coverageDates` and `coverageComplete: true`; genuinely empty publisher results count as checked dates. UTC ICS timestamps, exact publisher branch coordinates, and cancellation handling remain unchanged.

Full live monthly validation on 2026-09-07 UTC collected 843 raw event/tombstone records across September 6–October 5 using 1,860 requests in 546 seconds. A separate listing-only verification confirmed both date-filter echoes on all 49 listing pages for those 30 dates (916 listing links; busiest day 54 events), without repeating detail/calendar fetches.
